core.title: Every endpoint declared in markup by a declarative request construct has a test
core.given: A scan unit (the profile's scan scope) containing test files and markup that declares endpoints via the stack's declarative request constructs
core.when: The scan unit is scanned: every endpoint declared in markup, changed or not, is checked against the scan unit's tests
core.then: Every endpoint declared in markup by a declarative request construct MUST be exercised by at least one test in the same scan unit.
prefer: Write a test exercising the declared endpoint; a literal reference to it in a test file's text, or a static-prefix match for a dynamic segment, is sufficient coverage evidence for the checker.
If the surface is not real, delete the declaration instead.
Read the markup as the route space: a declarative request construct in markup IS the request.
avoid: Declaring an endpoint in markup with no test, so a new server surface exists that nothing records.
Reporting endpoints uncovered on a scan unit that contains no tests at all.
unless: The scan unit contains no test files: skip it entirely.
A dynamic segment matches on its static prefix (a test hitting a concrete value covers the templated endpoint).
An endpoint declared as an absolute URL is the same-origin declaration rule's finding, not this rule's.
core.why: An endpoint declared in markup is not an enumerable router-table entry, so the route space grows and is forgotten easily; this rule notices new surfaces. A coverage claim needs a suite to measure against, so without tests it stays silent.
evidence: The endpoint-coverage check reports no declared endpoint that no test file in the same scan unit mentions.
For each endpoint declared in markup in the scan unit (changed or not), a test file in the same scan unit references it literally or up to a dynamic segment.
verification: The check scans the whole scan unit (not a diff): it collects every endpoint declared by a declarative request construct in markup and in source, collects the text of every test file in the same scan unit, and reports an endpoint no test mentions.
Matching: a literal match counts, as does a match up to a dynamic segment (static-prefix match), so a test hitting a concrete value covers the templated endpoint.

Coverage no-op: when a scan unit holds markup but no test files, the check emits nothing rather than report every endpoint uncovered. A coverage rule needs both sides; a source-only scan is not evidence of a missing test; and a tester-persona rule must not produce findings on a tree containing no tests. The no-op matters as much as the check.

Route space is read where the stack honestly declares its endpoints — here the markup, because the declarative request construct IS the request — not from a plan artifact; reading markup rather than a plan file is not a boundary violation.
Endpoints declared as absolute URLs are skipped; they are the same-origin declaration rule's finding, not this check's.
Severity 2; disposition strict: fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

values: an endpoint declared in markup is not mentioned by any test in the same scan unit

fires: Presentation markup gains a declared endpoint and no test file in the same scan unit mentions it.
An existing, unchanged markup file in a scan unit that contains tests declares an endpoint that no test file mentions.
A scan unit with tests has a declared endpoint with a dynamic segment and no test hits any concrete path under its static prefix.
doesNotFire: The scan unit contains markup but no test files at all (coverage no-op).
A test hits a concrete value for a templated endpoint with a dynamic segment.
The declared endpoint is an absolute URL (the same-origin declaration rule's finding).

proposedKeys.meaning: The declarative markup constructs (hypermedia verb attributes) whose occurrence in markup declares an endpoint; an endpoint-coverage rule enumerates every occurrence as part of the route space.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.destructive_request and idiom.mutation_requests cover only destructive and mutating constructs; no existing key covers the full endpoint-declaring set including plain reads (hx-get), which a coverage check must enumerate.

neutralityNotes: The core speaks of 'declarative request constructs' and 'scan units', taking the concrete verb-attribute set (proposed key idiom.endpoint_declarations), the markup kinds and the scan scope from the profile. Identifying which files inside a scan unit count as tests is left to the realization: bun.json says only 'test file' / file_kind 'test', so no exact Bun suffix value exists for suffix.unit_test/acceptance_test and no such requirement was asserted. Coverage evidence is what the checker accepts — a literal mention in test-file text or a static-prefix match — and the core's prefer entry deliberately recommends, but does not require, that the test actually issue the request. The absolute-URL exclusion hands off to the same-origin declaration rule; the stack's rule id (coder.htmx.verb-endpoint-same-origin) stays bunOnly, with the neutral counterpart referred to generically. The dynamic-segment/static-prefix matching is stated as a generic routing concept; its concrete syntax stays with the realization. Severity 2 and the strict disposition are carried in core:verification, not the profile.
